Q: Creating a view based on an rvalue container A:

The question is whether this code triggers undefined behavior?

No. This is well-defined behavior.

When the pr value vector is applied to the range adaptor, it is implicitly converted into an owning_view before being applied, and its data ownership is transferred to the owning_view.

Therefore, the vw itself now holds the data and is not dangling.

It's important to note that the owning_view is a move-only view, so you must move it to transfer data ownership again:

auto vw = get_vec() | std::views::take(3);

auto vw2 =           vw  | std::views::take(5); // not ok
auto vw2 = std::move(vw) | std::views::take(5); // this is ok

Q: Approximate Matching and Replacement in Text R A:

Some agrep examples:

agrep("lasy", "1 lazy 2")
agrep("lasy", "1 lazy 2", max = list(sub = 0))
agrep("laysy", c("1 lazy", "1", "1 LAZY"), max = 2)
agrep("laysy", c("1 lazy", "1", "1 LAZY"), max = 2, value = TRUE)
agrep("laysy", c("1 lazy", "1", "1 LAZY"), max = 2, ignore.case = TRUE)

agrep is in base. If you load stringdist you can calculate string-distance using Jarro-Winkler with (you guessed) stringdist or if you're lazy you can just use ain or amatch. For my purposes, I tend to use Damerau–Levenshtein (method="dl") more, but your mileage might vary.

Just make sure to read up on exactly how the algorithm's parameters work before you use it (i.e. set your p, q and maxDist values to levels that make sense given what you're doing)

Q: vite:build-html EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read A:

For me this error came from the link tag on my index.html

<link rel="canonical" href="/" />

All you have to do is set an absolute path for the href or simply remove it, this might be a rare case though because I couldn't find a post that referenced this solution. Hope it helps someone out, and saves you some time.

Q: Creating a tibble with specific information pulled out A:

This doesn't strike me as a "Tooling" question but rather a standard "How do I...?" question, but as such it is framed as a discussion rather than something that can use the typical "Question" / "Answer(s)" structure.

I would suggest something like:

tibble(decimal_time = as.numeric(time(co2)), # as.numeric strips the tsp attribute
                                             # which'd prevent date_decimal from working
                                             # see  `?time`
       co2_ppm = co2,
       year = floor(decimal_time),
       date = date_decimal(decimal_time))
  summarize(mean_co2 = mean(co2_ppm), .by = year)

Q: How do you know if you truly understand a concept? A:

The advice my grandfather always gave me was just build, start building and keep building. Think of a weird thing to program, program it. If you get stuck go over your notes and re-learn. As a Computer Science student myself I literally just program - it's so simple to say but think of a concept, make a program revolving around it, do some weird stuff with the concept. Try set challenges to not look up stuff, just get an error and figure it out etc.
